Class Navigator

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.robotics.navigation.Navigator
All Implemented Interfaces:
WaypointListener
public final class Navigator extends Object implements WaypointListener
Drives a robot through a path of Waypoints, as leJOS's Navigator does: for each waypoint it turns to face the point, travels to it, and turns to the waypoint's heading when one is required. It runs on a virtual thread of its own, started by the first followPath(), so the program can watch, stop() it or waitForStop().

The pose is the navigator's own, in Cartesian millimetres and degrees (see Pose). Its heading is always the DirectionFinder's, a gyroscope's for instance, so a turn that came out a few degrees short or long, or a travel that drifted, is in the pose as it happened. Its position advances by the distance each travel covered, along the heading the robot had on the way. Each leg is planned from that measured pose, and a robot that ends a leg further from the point than the waypoint's tolerance drives another leg, at most MAX_LEGS per waypoint: leJOS plans once and never checks.

The pilot does the moves: one that steers with the heading while it travels, such as a GyroDifferentialPilot, or one that corrects it between moves, such as a GyroRegulatedDifferentialDrive. The path lives in an array the program allocates, new Waypoint[4] for four waypoints, since a board's arrays have sizes known when the program is compiled; a waypoint is removed once reached. Create the navigator once at startup; driving the path allocates nothing.

As a WaypointListener, it takes its path from a planner, as leJOS's does: the planner sends each waypoint with addWaypoint(Waypoint) and then pathGenerated(), which starts or resumes following it. A planner that listens to the navigator can re-plan from inside NavigationListener.pathInterrupted(Waypoint, Pose, int): there, lastOutcome() says why the leg ended, and clearPath(), addWaypoint(Waypoint) and pathGenerated() can be called on the navigator's own thread. DetourPlanner drives around obstacles that way.
